scene.note: Dates written as text become dates the laptop can count with, and go out again written in full.

steps.note: A time from the sign-out book comes in as text.
A format says which part of the text is the day, the month, the year, the hour and the minute.
Out comes a date with its time of day, ready to count with.
The date of the last check comes from the kit sheet, and today is handed in.
The text becomes a date, and one date is taken from the other.
Dougie gets the days since the check as a plain number.
The date of a check comes in as three numbers, with the days until the next one.
The numbers make a date, and the days are added as a gap, months and leap years counted for you.
Dougie gets the date the next check is due.
A date with its time goes in.
The day of the week and the month become names from the file's own lists.
The council gets one line written in full, the time in hours and minutes.
